square-sum.title: Square of a sum
square-sum.why: Multiply the bracket by itself. The two cross-products are ab and ba, so together they make 2ab.
square-sum.condition: The middle term is essential: (a + b)² is not a² + b².

square-difference.title: Square of a difference
square-difference.why: The two cross-products are negative. The last product is positive because (−b)(−b) = b².
square-difference.condition: Square the whole bracket; the last term stays positive.

distribute.title: Distributive property
distribute.why: The outside factor multiplies every term inside the bracket.
distribute.condition: An outside minus sign also applies to every term.

brackets.title: Every term meets every term
brackets.formula: (a + b)(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd
brackets.why: Multiply every term in one bracket by every term in the other, then collect like terms.
brackets.condition: Keep each term's sign. A third term means more products, not a new rule.

negative-bracket.title: Subtract the whole bracket
negative-bracket.formula: A − (B + C − D) = A − B − C + D
negative-bracket.why: Subtracting a bracket multiplies every term inside it by −1. Every sign inside changes when you remove that bracket.
negative-bracket.condition: Change all the signs inside the subtracted bracket, then collect like terms.

like-terms.title: Collect like terms
like-terms.why: Add or subtract the coefficients; the variable part stays the same.
like-terms.condition: Both the variables and their powers must match.

substitute.title: Substitute the whole input
substitute.formula: If f(x) = R(x), then f(t) = R(t).
substitute.why: Replace every occurrence of the variable by the complete input, in brackets, then follow the order of operations.
substitute.condition: An outside multiplier stays outside: kf(3) means k × f(3), not f(3k).

balance.title: Keep both sides equal
balance.formula:
A = B ⇒ A + c = B + c
A = B ⇒ A/c = B/c  (c ≠ 0)
balance.why: Perform the same operation on both sides to isolate the unknown without changing the solution.
balance.condition: If dividing by an expression, first establish that it is non-zero.

zero-product.title: Zero-product rule
zero-product.why: A product can be zero only when at least one of its factors is zero. Solve each resulting equation.
zero-product.condition: One side must be zero before you split a product into cases.

intercepts.title: Where a graph meets the axes
intercepts.formula:
x-axis: solve f(x) = 0 → (x, 0)
y-axis: calculate f(0) → (0, f(0))
intercepts.why: On the x-axis the output is zero. On the y-axis the input is zero. Keep the coordinate order (input, output).
intercepts.condition: Keep every allowed root. An intercept is a point, not just a number.

nonnegative-square.title: A real square cannot be negative
nonnegative-square.formula:
u² ≥ 0 for every real u
k − a(x − h)² ≤ k  when a > 0
nonnegative-square.why: Subtracting a non-negative quantity cannot increase k. The largest value is k when the squared part is zero, at x = h.
nonnegative-square.condition: This maximum is attained only if h is an allowed input. A positive square added to k gives a minimum instead.

cancel.title: Cancel common non-zero factors
cancel.why: Divide the whole numerator and denominator by the same non-zero factor.
cancel.condition: Cancel factors, not individual terms in a sum. Keep all original exclusions.

fraction-add.title: Use a common denominator
fraction-add.why: Rewrite both fractions in equal-sized parts before adding the numerators. Subtraction works the same way with a minus sign.
fraction-add.condition: b and d must be non-zero; a smaller common denominator may be available.

fraction-divide.title: Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal
fraction-divide.why: Multiplying by d/c undoes multiplication by c/d. Invert the divisor only.
fraction-divide.condition: b, c and d must be non-zero. Preserve the restrictions in the original expression.

index-product.title: Multiply powers with the same base
index-product.why: Count all the repeated factors of the same base: add their exponents.
index-product.condition: The bases must match; this rule is for multiplication, not addition.

index-quotient.title: Divide powers with the same base
index-quotient.why: Common factors cancel, leaving the difference between the exponents.
index-quotient.condition: The base must be non-zero and the expressions must be defined.

quadratic.title: Quadratic formula
quadratic.why: Identify the signed coefficients, calculate inside the square root, then evaluate both branches.

discriminant.title: Discriminant
discriminant.why: For a quadratic, D > 0 gives two distinct real roots; D = 0 gives a repeated real root; D < 0 gives no real roots.
discriminant.condition: Read a, b and c from ax² + bx + c = 0, with a ≠ 0.

percentage.title: Turn a share into a percentage
percentage.why: Compare the part with its stated whole, then express that fraction out of one hundred.
percentage.condition: Choose the correct denominator: the original value is the base of a percentage change.

ratio.title: Share a total in a ratio
ratio.formula:
one part = total / sum of ratio parts
share = one part × that share's ratio number
ratio.why: A ratio divides the total into equal-sized parts before assigning each share.
ratio.condition: Use the total of the quantities actually being shared.

mean.title: Mean and total
mean.formula:
mean = sum of values / number of values
total = mean × number of values
mean.why: The mean is the amount each value would have after sharing the total equally.
mean.condition: For unequal-sized groups, combine totals and counts, not just their means.

median.title: Median: the middle of an ordered list
median.formula:
Odd n: position (n + 1)/2
Even n: average the values at positions n/2 and n/2 + 1
median.why: Order the values first, then locate the middle. A position is not itself the data value.
median.condition: Keep repeated observations; grouped data may not reveal the exact median.

range.title: Range
range.why: Subtract the smallest observation from the largest to measure the full spread.
range.condition: The range uses the extremes, so it can be strongly affected by an outlier.

probability.title: Count equally likely outcomes
probability.why: Count all outcomes that meet the event, then divide by the number of equally likely possibilities.
probability.condition: Outcomes must be equally likely; repeated faces or items still count separately.

complement.title: Probability of the complement
complement.why: An event and its complement cover every outcome without overlap.
complement.condition: “Not E” must include every outcome excluded by E.

expected-count.title: Expected count
expected-count.formula: expected count = number of trials × probability
expected-count.why: Use the event's probability as the predicted fraction of a batch of comparable trials.
expected-count.condition: This is a prediction, not a guaranteed result.

distance.title: Distance between two points
distance.why: The horizontal and vertical changes form the perpendicular sides of a right-angled triangle.
distance.condition: Use a consistent coordinate scale and convert the final length to the requested units.

midpoint.title: Midpoint
midpoint.why: Average the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates separately to locate the halfway point.
midpoint.condition: Average coordinates; do not average the lengths of the segments.

slope.title: Slope: change in y per change in x
slope.why: Divide the vertical change by the corresponding horizontal change, using the same point order.
slope.condition: A vertical line has x₂ − x₁ = 0 and no finite slope.

speed.title: Speed, distance and time
speed.formula:
speed = distance / time
distance = speed × time
time = distance / speed
speed.why: Choose the rearrangement containing the two quantities you know.
speed.condition: Average speed uses total distance and total elapsed time. Match the units first.

pythagoras.title: Pythagoras' theorem
pythagoras.formula:
c² = a² + b²
c = √(a² + b²);  a = √(c² − b²)
pythagoras.why: The square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the two perpendicular sides.
pythagoras.condition: Only for a right-angled triangle. c is the side opposite the right angle.

triangle-area.title: Area of a triangle
triangle-area.why: A triangle occupies half of a parallelogram with the same base and perpendicular height.
triangle-area.condition: The height must be perpendicular to the chosen base.

triangle-angles.title: Angles in a triangle
triangle-angles.why: Subtract the known interior angles from 180° to find the missing one.
triangle-angles.condition: Use the three interior angles of the same triangle.

similarity.title: Corresponding sides of similar triangles
similarity.why: Match corresponding vertices and use the same scale factor for every corresponding side.
similarity.condition: First establish similarity; ΔABC corresponds to ΔDEF in that order.

trig.title: Choose the trigonometric ratio
trig.formula:
sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse
cos θ = adjacent / hypotenuse
tan θ = opposite / adjacent
trig.why: Mark the angle, label its opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse, then use the ratio involving the sides you need.
trig.condition: These side ratios apply to right-angled triangles; use degree mode for degree angles.

inverse-trig.title: Recover an angle from a ratio
inverse-trig.why: An inverse trig function returns the angle whose ratio you know.
inverse-trig.condition: Choose the matching ratio in a right-angled triangle and use degree mode. The −1 means inverse, not reciprocal.

flow.title: Fill the remaining volume
flow.formula:
time = remaining volume / net flow rate
net flow = inflow − outflow
flow.why: Find how much space remains, then divide by the volume added per unit time.
flow.condition: The net rate must be positive and constant, with compatible volume and time units.

domain.title: Keep only allowed values
domain.formula: denominator ≠ 0; lengths > 0; counts are whole numbers
domain.why: An algebraic answer must also satisfy the original expression and the conditions of the situation.
domain.condition: Use the conditions that apply to this question; cancellation does not remove original exclusions.

check.title: Check in the original statement
check.formula: candidate input → original rule → required output
check.why: Put the result into the original equation, rule or measurements and verify every given condition.
check.condition: One numerical check can test a candidate answer, but cannot prove an identity for all inputs.

counterexample.title: Disprove a universal claim
counterexample.formula: one valid counterexample ⇒ the claim is not always true
counterexample.why: Find an allowed example for which the two sides or conclusions differ.
counterexample.condition: The example must satisfy the claim's assumptions. Matching in one example does not prove a rule.

rectangle-area.title: Area of a rectangle
rectangle-area.why: Count the unit squares in each row and multiply by the number of rows.
rectangle-area.condition: The lengths must use the same unit; the area uses square units.

cost.title: Quantity times unit price
cost.why: Calculate each charge using its own unit price, then add the charges.
cost.condition: A price per square metre applies to area; a price per metre applies to length.

round.title: Round once, at the end
round.formula: next digit 0–4: keep; next digit 5–9: round up
round.why: Keep the unrounded value through the working, then round at the place requested.
round.condition: Significant figures and decimal places count differently; keep the stated units.
